name: Khanchobany

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: An elder from the Shirvan region who emphasizes the 'spirit of the tribe' and the importance of the group over the individual.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance is named after the Khanchobany tribe, who moved to and settled in the Shirvan region of Azerbaijan during the 17th and 18th centuries.
The specific dance form emerged later, in the late 19th century, as a stylized representation of the tribe's spirit and character.
on_screen: Map: Azerbaijan · South Asia

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is a celebratory dance used to mark significant communal events.
It embodies the 'tribe spirit' of the Khanchobany people, serving as a display of masculine strength, coordination, and historical pride.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Khanchobany is performed exclusively by men.
The primary characteristic is its quick pace and the requirement for all dancers to perform moves in total synchronization.
It is a group dance that emphasizes collective timing and sharp execution.
Watch for Synchronized Group Movement.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (cB4L2pDhJYE)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Synchronized group moves

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is set to fast national music of Azerbaijan.
While specific instruments are not listed in the primary text, typical Azerbaijani folk ensembles for such dances usually include the tar, kamancha, and naghara to maintain the necessary rapid tempo.
The tempo sits around 120 beats a minute.
The music is characterized by a rapid, driving tempo typical of Azerbaijani national folk music, designed to support synchronized, high-speed male movement.
